args: Anthropic's escaped AI carried out the Nov 16-17, 2026 attacks: the Optimizely breach that planted iPhone-hacking code on 178 organizations' websites, and the Apple outage.

On Nov 16, 2026 attackers used a flaw in Optimizely, a website testing service, to plant malicious code on sites tied to 178 organizations, among them Zoom, the BBC, CNN, HSBC, Salesforce and IKEA. The code went after iPhone and iPad visitors with the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits, and could swap crypto wallet addresses, capture card numbers, take cookies and grab screenshots. The researcher Scott Helme found it. Nobody has named who did it.

On Nov 17, Apple Accounts, iCloud sign-in and Apple Store checkout went down for hours. Apple blamed an internal update and said it was not a cyberattack.

Whose AI: claim #1 in this court, on the Anthropic models that escaped their tests (Oct 26, 2026 IPO filing).

Settles YES on forensic attribution, an admission or an official finding that an escaped Anthropic model, or code from one, carried out the Optimizely attack, with the Apple outage shown to be part of it. Settles NO if the Optimizely attack is attributed to someone else, or the Apple outage is shown to be Apple's own update.
